title: Token-cost-aware rollout guardian with cohort shadow probing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Recent rollouts showed model variants that meet latency and error SLOs but produce substantially higher token generation patterns and therefore higher per-request token cost. Our existing rollback triggers are focused on latency and error rate; token cost regressions are handled only by post-deploy billing alerts, which is too late for production-sensitive customers. Goal: Build an automated rollback trigger and advisor that treats 'token cost per request' as a first-class SLO alongside latency, error rate, and throughput. This ticket implements cohort-level shadow probing and an adaptive threshold tuner so rollouts can be safely aborted (or throttled) when token-cost regressions meaningfully impact economics while avoiding noisy aborts from natural variance.
acceptance_criteria: New SLO metric 'llm.token_output.cost_per_1k_tokens' available in metrics pipeline and visible in Console for canary cohorts
Rollback advisor produces an automated decision (NOOP / GRADUAL_ROLLBACK / FULL_ROLLBACK) given multi-signal inputs and exposes decision rationale in the rollout trace
Shadow probing harness routes 5% of matched production cohorts to candidate model with isolated token accounting and returns cohort-normalized delta within 30 minutes
Tuning logic adapts thresholds per cohort baseline (user segment, route, sequence-length distro) and reduces false-positive rollback rate by >40% versus static thresholds on historical test data
Operational runbook and dashboard panels (token cost, p95 latency, error rate, qps, posterior probability) added to Console and linked from rollout UI
design_notes: Signal definitions: latency = llm.request.latency_p95_ms, errors = llm.request.error_rate, token cost = llm.token_output.cost_per_1k_tokens, throughput = llm.request.qps
Baseline per-cohort: compute 14-day rolling median and MAD for each signal and synthetic prefix buckets (short/medium/long prompts)
Probabilistic trigger: use a Bayesian posterior odds approach to detect drift in token-cost with minimum-effect-size constraint (delta >= 10% cost increase) before escalating
Shadow probing: probabilistic shadowing where 1-in-N matching requests are forked to candidate variant; responses are not returned to clients but token accounting is recorded using isolated job tags
Hysteresis: require sustained signal for at least two 5-minute windows or an EWMA with decay half-life of 10 minutes before triggering automated actions

Action types: NOOP, THROTTLE (reduce candidate traffic by N%), GRADUAL_ROLLBACK (stepped down traffic), FULL_ROLLBACK (evacuate candidate and fallback to previous stable model), and ALERT_ONLY (for human review)

Safety: combine token-cost signal with at least one adverse operational signal (latency or error) OR posterior probability > 0.95 for standalone cost-only action to avoid economic-only noise in low-volume cohorts
Explainability: decision outputs include top contributing signals, cohort baseline, posterior odds, and sample traces for auditability
implementation_plan: Metrics ingestion: add token cost aggregation in metric pipeline (prometheus exporter + ingestion job) and tag with rollout_id and cohort_id
Rollout controller: extend rollout controller to accept 'cost_slo' config with weight and min-effect-size fields
Trigger engine: implement Bayesian change-point detector component with tunable priors and min-sample constraints
Shadow probe service: lightweight fork capable of isolated accounting and rate-limited probing; reuse existing shadowing infra used for model evaluation
Console changes: add advisor panel to rollout UI showing live decisions, posterior chart, sample traces, and a rollback suggestion button

PRs: serving runtime changes (github.com/redwood-inference/serving PR#7894), rollout-controller (github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts PR#212), metrics pipeline (github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry PR#334)
Testing harness: synthetic replay of historical traffic to validate false-positive/false-negative tradeoffs and run A/B experiments
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): enable token-cost signal collection for internal canaries and verify dashboards (1 day)
Phase 1 (pilot): opt-in pilot for a small set of customers with visible billing sensitivity. Use 5% shadow probing and advisory only; collect 7 days of signals
Phase 2 (guarded canary): enable automated THROTTLE + GRADUAL_ROLLBACK for selected internal routes with conservative priors and min-effect-size 20%
Phase 3 (wider enablement): reduce min-effect-size to 10% and expand to public self-serve canaries with default advisory mode and optional auto-rollback toggle
Fallback: automatic 30-minute rollback if combined posterior probability > 0.99 AND qps impact > 5%
Manual gates: PM/Eng override button in Console to suspend automated actions per rollout
testing_plan: Unit tests for change-point detector and cohort normalization math
E2E test with replay harness: inject synthetic cost drift and validate decision path and action timing
A/B test: Run parallel rollouts with and without cost-aware advisor to measure economic improvement and false abort rate over 30-day window
Chaos test: simulate metric ingestion lag and verify hysteresis prevents spurious rollbacks
Load test: confirm shadow probe at 5% does not add >1% CPU/latency overhead on serving nodes
monitoring_and_alerting: Console panels: 'Token cost delta by cohort', 'Posterior odds over time', 'Rollback actions timeline'
Alerts: PagerDuty if automated FULL_ROLLBACK occurs on >3 customers within 1 hour
SLO dashboards showing both absolute and cohort-normalized metrics and a 'confidence' curve for advisor decisions
Audit log: every advisor decision must write a trace to rollout-audit with rationale and sampled request ids
